'''Yamashiro-Kuga no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''yamashiro no kuga no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''yamashiro no kuga kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled [[#Territory|Yamashiro-Kuga Province]].

== Overview ==
A kuni no miyatsuko named in the shrine traditions of {{ill|Kuga Shrine|ja|久我神社|qid=Q11369375}}, but not recorded in the "{{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}}" or other major sources. Other kuni no miyatsuko also omitted from the Kokuzō Hongi (such as the {{ill|Ōita no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|大分国造}} and {{ill|Chiba no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|千葉国造}}) similarly exist. The ''Yamashiro no Kuni Fudoki'' (extant fragment) does record that {{ill|Takenotsunomi-no-Mikoto|ja|建角身命}} took his seat on the northern mountains of '''Kuga Province'''.

=== Ancestry ===
*The "Jindai Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'' transmits that '''{{ill|Amenokamutachi-no-Mikoto|ja|天神立命}}''' was the ancestor of the Yamashiro-Kuga-no-Atai.
*The "Tenshin Hongi" of the ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'' records that Amenokamutachi-no-Mikoto, who accompanied {{ill|Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|ja|饒速日命}}, was the ancestor of the Yamashiro-Kuga-no-Atai, while Amenoyohira-no-Mikoto (a miscopying of Amenoyoo-no-Mikoto) was the ancestor of the Kuga-no-Atai.
*In the founding tradition of Kuga Shrine, the enshrined deity '''Kogamayotsugi-no-Kami''' is said to be the ancestral deity of the Yamashiro-Kuga no Kuni no Miyatsuko. Today Kuga Shrine enshrines {{ill|Takenotsunomi-no-Mikoto|ja|建角身命}}, {{ill|Tamayori-hime|ja|タマヨリビメ|lt=Tamayori-hime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Wakeikazuchi-no-Kami|ja|別雷神}}.

=== Clan ===
'''Yamashiro-Kuga clan''' (''yamashiro no kuga-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}), also written simply Kuga clan. Amenokamutachi-no-Mikoto (Ame-no-Oshitatsu-no-Mikoto) is recorded in the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}}'' as ancestor of the Eki-no-Atai of {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}} Shinbetsu and of the Katsuragi-no-Atai of {{ill|Settsu Province|ja|摂津国}} undetermined-surnames, and is of the same kin as the {{ill|Kamo-no-Agatanushi clan|ja|賀茂県主氏}} and the {{ill|Katsuragi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|葛城国造}}. In Yamashiro Province, alongside the Kuga-no-Atai, the Imaki-no-Atai, Awata-no-Atai, and Nishikoribe-no-Atai are also identifiable as related to the kuni no miyatsuko clan.{{Sfn|Hōga Toshio|2021|pp=69–71}}

== Base ==
Around present-day Kuga district in {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都市|lt=Kyoto City}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府}}. {{ill|Kuga Shrine|ja|久我神社|qid=Q11369375}} and the place name Kuga remain today.

== Tutelary deity ==
'''{{ill|Kuga Shrine (Fushimi)|ja|久我神社 (京都市伏見区)|lt=Kuga Shrine}}''', identified as the {{ill|shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} Kuga Shrine in {{ill|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|ja|伏見区|lt=Fushimi Ward}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture.

=== Related shrines ===
; {{ill|Kuga Shrine (Kita-ku, Kyoto)|ja|久我神社 (京都市北区)|lt=Kuga Shrine}} (''kuga jinja'')
: A {{ill|shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} of {{ill|Atago District|ja|愛宕郡}}, located in {{ill|Kita-ku, Kyoto|ja|北区 (京都市)|lt=Kita-ku}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. Today it is an external auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Kamigamo Shrine|ja|賀茂別雷神社}}.

=== Tomb ===
; {{ill|Egesanyama Kofun|ja|恵解山古墳}}
: A {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} in Shōryūji and Kugai, {{ill|Nagaokakyō, Kyoto|ja|長岡京市|lt=Nagaokakyō City}}, Kyoto Prefecture, with a mound 120 meters long; thought to have been built in the early {{ill|5th century|ja|5世紀}}.
